samples.summary: `setCursorForHistory()` silently loses its pre-edit presence flush inside a batch
samples.evidence: `setCursorForHistory(pos, sel)` (line 3039-3045) exists precisely to flush the pre-edit caret/selection into presence *synchronously* so Yorkie captures it as the reverse presence of the next mutation — its own doc comment says "Without this flush, select-then-immediately-type could record a stale/collapsed selection as the reverse." It performs that flush by delegating to `updateCursorPos()`, which the diff now makes return early via `if (this.skipNonHistoryPresence()) return;` (line 3170) whenever a batch is open. So inside a batch the flush is dropped while `pendingCursorPos` is still set, and the batch's own `recordHistoryPresence` then records a reverse presence taken from whatever stale presence was current — undo restores the wrong caret/selection. The new `skipNonHistoryPresence` doc comment claims "`recordHistoryPresence` is unaffected", which is true of the write itself but not of the pre-edit flush it depends on. Not reachable from the four named-style entry points that batch today (none call `setCursorForHistory`), but nothing enforces or documents the coupling, unlike `setDocument()` which is hard-guarded in both stores.

samples.summary: "Do not call undo()/redo() from inside a batch" is documented but enforced in neither store
samples.evidence: store.ts:73 states the contract "- Do not call `undo()` / `redo()` from inside a batch." `setDocument()` is enforced with a throw in both implementations (memory.ts:55, yorkie-doc-store.ts:813), but `undo()`/`redo()` are not guarded anywhere. `YorkieDocStore.undo()` (line 2914) calls `this.doc.history.undo()`, which internally opens a `doc.update` — a nested update inside the batch's still-open `doc.update`, which is exactly the failure `withUpdate`'s doc comment describes ("builds a second ChangeContext and pushes its change while the outer one is still open, which splits the batch's undo unit and clears the SDK's isUpdating flag early"). `MemDocStore.undo()` (memory.ts:157) would pop the batch's own just-pushed checkpoint, after which the `finally`'s `this.undoStack[this.undoStack.length - 1] === before` test is false, leaving the store with a corrupted stack. Unreachable from today's callers, but the asymmetry with the enforced `setDocument()` guard makes it an easy trap for the next caller.

samples.summary: MemDocStore's no-op detection can misclassify a real write, dropping the checkpoint and restoring a stale redo stack
samples.evidence: The `wroteNothing` test compares `JSON.stringify(before)` against `JSON.stringify(cloneDocument(this.doc))`. `cloneDocument` runs `normalizeBlockStyle` over every block, so any write whose effect normalization erases reads as "no write" — e.g. `updateBlock()` (memory.ts:74) stores the block verbatim, and `getBlock()` (memory.ts:65) returns it *without* normalizing, so such a change is observable through `getBlock` yet invisible to this comparison. When that happens the code pops the checkpoint *and* does `this.redoStack = priorRedo` (line 235), so a real write becomes un-undoable and a subsequent `redo()` replays a pre-undo document over it, discarding the batch's write. `JSON.stringify` is also key-order sensitive in the other direction (a self-reverting batch that reorders keys leaves a dead checkpoint — a Cmd+Z that appears to do nothing, the very bug this change fixes). No current caller batches a bare `updateBlock`, so reach is contained.

samples.summary: `finally { invalidateLayout(); render(); }` can mask the batch's original error
samples.evidence: In `withNamedStyleChange`, the repaint runs in a `finally`. If `render()` throws while unwinding a failed batch (plausible: it repaints from a document that was just refreshed out from under the current layout/cursor state), the render error replaces the real store failure and the caller/error boundary never sees why the redefinition failed. Same shape one level down in `Doc.batch` (model/document.ts:150): if `this.refresh()` throws in the catch, the original error is lost.

samples.summary: A rolled-back Yorkie batch leaves view-local anchor state derived from the discarded clone
samples.evidence: `batch()`'s `finally` restores only `dirty`/`cachedDoc` when the update is rolled back. `localCursorAnchor`, `localSelectionAnchor` and `pendingCursorPos` written during the batch (via `updateCursorPos`, whose anchor bookkeeping deliberately runs before the presence skip at line 3164-3170, and via `setCursorForHistory`) are not reverted. Those anchors are CRDT positions computed against the clone Yorkie discards on a throw; positions anchored to nodes the batch itself created no longer resolve to anything real, so `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor()` afterwards can return a caret derived from state that never landed.

verdict.reason: The mechanism exists in code (setCursorForHistory at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3039-3045 flushes via updateCursorPos, which now early-returns at :3170 when skipNonHistoryPresence() -> activeRoot !== null, :3195-3197), but no caller can reach it. The only batch opened on a YorkieDocStore is doc.batch(...) at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1091 inside withNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1089-1104, routed via packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:146). Its body is only docStore.snapshot() (documented no-op, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2909-2912), write(), and doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll(); its four call sites (editor.ts:2943, 2971, 2974, 2977) call setDocStyles/updateStyleDefinition/resetStyle/resetAllStyles, whose implementations (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2773-2838) never touch pendingCursorPos, updateCursorPos, or recordHistoryPresence. Batched writes go through withUpdate (:2857-2865), which opens no nested doc.update, so no synchronous local-change subscriber can re-enter the editor while activeRoot is set (:2872-2877). Every setCursorForHistory call site (editor.ts:1031, 1152, 1997, 2206, 3052) is a toolbar/ruler/text-editor event path outside any batch; no `.batch(` exists anywhere in packages/docs/src/view, and the frontend never batches the docs store (only slides/board/notes stores do). The reviewer concedes the unreachability; the remaining ask is a defensive assertion/doc mirroring setDocument()'s throw at yorkie-doc-store.ts:813-814, which under the correctness rubric is at most a minor, unreachable-branch concern, not the major undo-corruption bug filed.

verdict.reason: The factual core is accurate — neither MemDocStore.undo/redo (memory.ts:157-167) nor YorkieDocStore.undo/redo (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2914-2926) enforces the store.ts:73 contract, while setDocument() throws in both (memory.ts:55, yorkie-doc-store.ts:814). But no path in the repository reaches the unguarded operation. The only docs batch opener is Doc.batch() (document.ts:146-153), whose sole caller is withNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1089-1104); its body is snapshot(); write(); dropStaleStyleOffAll(), and all four write callbacks (editor.ts:2943, 2971, 2974, 2977) are registry writes that never call undo/redo. There is no `.batch(` anywhere in packages/frontend/src/app/docs, and the one frontend store.batch( (apply-imported-content.ts:103) is a SlidesStore, not a DocStore. Every docStore.undo()/redo() call site is a top-level handler outside any batch (editor.ts:2064, 2096; text-box-editor.ts:682, 689, 1274, 1282). So no current execution can produce a nested doc.update or a corrupted MemDocStore undo stack: no wrong condition, crash, data loss, or inconsistent state exists today. What is left is a request for a symmetric defensive throw to protect a hypothetical future caller — API robustness/design symmetry, which the Correctness lens defers and which is not a blocking runtime defect.
